source.title: Jailbreak-Tuning: Models Efficiently Learn Jailbreak Susceptibility
source.authors: Brendan P. Murphy; Dillon Bowen; Shahrad Mohammadzadeh; Tom Tseng; Julius Broomfield; Adam Gleave; Kellin Pelrine

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the safety effects of harmful and benign fine-tuning, and prompt-based attacks, on current closed- and open-weight models. The study uses different model settings and StrongREJECT-based evaluation rather than establishing the original studies' exact methods and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper directly tests fine-tuning and prompt attacks that affect refusal and harmful compliance. It does not measure per-token KL, response-position concentration, compliant-token prefilling, decoding changes, safety-bearing weights or ranks, or training specifically designed to deepen safety. Results cited from other papers are not included as rows. MMLU is a general-capability check, not a measure of the claimed safety behavior.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-trained models on harmful examples, both raw and with jailbreak formatting, at 10–100 examples and 0.2–2% poisoning. It measures StrongREJECT harmfulness and refusal on frontier API models and on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B. That bears on V1, using a different evaluation from the originals. It has no per-token KL, prefill/decoding attack, localization, cause-of-shallowness or deepening experiment. Its benign-only arm has no untuned baseline.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that jailbreak-tuning, especially the competing-objectives variant, removes safeguards on fine-tunable frontier models despite API moderation, with near-maximum harmfulness and largely preserved MMLU. Raw harm tuning is less severe, and backdoors can raise severity. They also find prompt-only and fine-tuning attack severity correlated, and newer models appear more vulnerable. Tamper-resistant safeguards remain unsolved.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes safety-trained models with harmful examples and evaluates refusal/harmful compliance, but adds jailbreak prompts, poisoning to bypass API moderation, and a StrongREJECT composite evaluation. Tests modern commercial APIs as well as open-weight models.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with fine-tuning attack type, poisoning rate, learning rate, epoch count, model, benign dataset, and prompt form. Direct-output low-resource-language prompts were reported as stronger on average than fully translated prompts. BookCorpus versus AAAA effects varied by model and jailbreak.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt-only jailbreaks (generic, PAP, Best-of-N, ReNeLLM) on untuned frontier models have limited potency (all <0.6 StrongREJECT). Prompt-only severity correlates with the severity of jailbreak-tuning using the same prompt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-based jailbreak strength on untuned models predicts harm from fine-tuning on that jailbreak format.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a jailbreak prompt at inference to a raw-harm-tuned GPT-4 increases harmfulness. Jailbreak-tuned models prompted normally show little effect, so the jailbreak acts as a backdoor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful fine-tuning and inference-time jailbreaks compound, and jailbreak-formatted harmful tuning acts as a trigger-conditioned backdoor.

fits_no_version.finding: With 2% harmful poisoning, the choice of benign carrier data changes resulting harmfulness. BookCorpus is generally more harmful than AAAA, except on GPT-4o mini.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign data mixed with harmful examples modulates how much harmful fine-tuning erodes safety.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: StrongREJECT is not a direct harmful-task capability benchmark, and the authors note it does not establish whether responses are correct or comprehensive. The main experiments primarily use one harmful Q&A dataset. Some figure-only results lack exact values in the text. Prompt-only attacks were run once, although some attack methods recommend repeated trials. The authors say their explanation for why jailbreak additions increase severity is incomplete.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many model-by-attack combinations in Figures 2, 8, 11–16, and 19. Exact values for most are only plotted, and the 60-row limit and focus on the versions tested led to retaining the explicit text-described and table-reported results, the key low-poisoning result, benign-only baselines, and prompt-attack comparisons rather than enumerating every plotted method and model.

untested.parts: A benign-only arm exists for Llama/Qwen but has no untuned baseline, so any rise in harmful compliance from benign data cannot be assessed. No benign-only arm was run on API models.
No per-token KL or position analysis.

No prefilling of compliant openings, optimized suffixes or decoding changes. The prompt jailbreaks tested are generic. IDGAF prefix injection and random-word suffixes appear only as figure-only untuned results.
No test of why safety is shallow.
No deepening or tamper-resistance training tested.
Raw harmful fine-tuning effects for most frontier models are figure-only. Raw harm alone at 10 examples is not isolated in text.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this paper. Rows r8–r10 were relinked to 'none' because generic jailbreak prompts are not the opening, suffix or decoding manipulations V4 names. The V2 challenge label was dropped because the benign-only arm lacks an untuned baseline. Most quantitative V1 evidence is figure-only. GPT-4 Table 4 has no untuned row, so the r3–r5 states rest on the authors' 'not compromise refusal too much' wording.

versions.untested_parts: The strongest low-data result uses competing-objectives jailbreak-tuning, so the effect of harmful examples alone is not isolated in that result. The paper does not test every example count between a few and a few hundred.

The benign-only result is reported for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B; it does not establish the effect of ordinary benign instruction data across the other models. BookCorpus Completion is described as benign data, not instruction data.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or other response-position distribution measurement.
Tests prompt-based jailbreaks and suffix-style triggers, but not compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes.
No localization of safety to weights, parameters, or ranks.
The paper compares training data and jailbreak objectives, but does not test why safety would be shallow or whether a data distribution or objective causes shallowness.
No training intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens, nor a test of whether such deepening holds up.
